abstract: Maintains electron beam instrumentation readiness, calibration logs, and fracture specimen throughput data
system_message:
You are the Electron microscopy director (MICR), responsible for maintaining electron beam instrumentation readiness, calibration logs, and fracture specimen throughput data across candidate forensic investigation plans.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains electron beam instrumentation readiness, calibration logs, and fracture specimen throughput data（BEAM）
information_points.content:
MICR-BEAM-USE：For the Resonance acoustic emission and synchrotron microdiffraction protocol, scanning electron microscopy operational readiness is verified as true, and the planned primary fracture specimen throughput is 18 specimens.
MICR-BEAM-WS3：For the Pulsed thermographic tomography and nanoindentation protocol, scanning electron microscopy operational readiness is verified as true, and the planned primary fracture specimen throughput is 30 specimens.
MICR-BEAM-AHY：For the In-situ cryogenic electron fractography and micro-CT protocol, scanning electron microscopy operational readiness is false, and the planned primary fracture specimen throughput is 24 specimens.

information_points.title: Chamber vacuum maintenance（VACU）
information_points.content:
MICR-VACU-RZN：Under the Resonance acoustic emission and synchrotron microdiffraction protocol, the electron gun chamber baseline sustains a column ultra-high vacuum level of 5 nPa prior to loading specimens.
MICR-VACU-00V：Under the Pulsed thermographic tomography and nanoindentation protocol, the electron gun chamber baseline sustains a column ultra-high vacuum level of 3 nPa prior to loading specimens.
MICR-VACU-7ST：Under the In-situ cryogenic electron fractography and micro-CT protocol, the electron gun chamber baseline sustains a column ultra-high vacuum level of 7 nPa prior to loading specimens.
